newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian coal town fights diarrhoea outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Romanian coal town fights diarrhoea outbreak.

text.p: A Romanian coal mining town has declared a "state of emergency" to cope with dilapidated sewers that caused a diarrhoea outbreak which killed six infants and put 250 in hospital.

Senior Health Ministry epidemiologist Adrian Streinu-Cercel said officials on Wednesday slapped a quarantine on the hospital in Rovinari, 300 km (180 miles) east of Bucharest, where the deaths occurred in the past two months.
"Sewage pipes are riddled with holes," he told Reuters. "Waste from sewers is dripping into the fresh water supply."
Patients and hospital staff were subjected to strict tests and each household in the town of 14,000 was to be issued with a water filter.

Outbreaks of diseases long eradicated in the West have gripped post-communist Romania, hit by steep falls in levels of health care, nutrition and general living standards. Poor hygiene and a breakdown in local services were other factors.

Forty mainly elderly people died of meningitis this year and 84 cases of cholera were recorded in 1995. Tuberculosis and hepatitis are on the rise and Romanian television reports deaths in hospitals almost nightly from a variety of viruses.
